title: Sugarcane Farmers Block Highways and Launch Padayatra Across Karnataka
seoTitle: Belagavi sugarcane farmers march and blockades

tea.why: Sugarcane farmers are protesting because a meeting with union ministers in Delhi failed to yield an immediate decision on sugarcane prices.
tea.want: Farmers demand higher prices for their produce, higher MSP, revised Fair and Remunerative Price, and Swaminathan Commission recommendations.
tea.changed: Oct 13: Farmers blocked national highways across Karnataka districts. Oct 18: Organisers announced the march is likely to temporarily end.

summary: Sugarcane farmers launched road blockades and a Hubballi Chalo padayatra across multiple districts in Karnataka, including Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, and Dharwad, causing major traffic disruptions on key routes like the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway. Organised by farmer groups and Hasiru Sene, the protests followed a failed meeting between farmer leaders and union ministers in Delhi regarding crop pricing. Protesters demanded higher prices for sugarcane, an increase in the Minimum Support Price, determination of the Fair and Remunerative Price, and the implementation of the Swaminathan Commission's recommendations. In response, Union Food Minister Pralhad Joshi appealed to farmers to withdraw the agitation and assured that the Centre would address their concerns, while police deployed additional personnel and held discussions with demonstrators.
demands: Higher prices for sugarcane and sugar
Revision of Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP)
Implementation of the Swaminathan Commission recommendations
State Advised Price of ₹1,000 per tonne of sugarcane supplied
response: Union Food Minister Pralhad Joshi appealed to farmers to withdraw their agitation, assuring them that the Centre would address their concerns. Police held discussions with protesters and deployed additional personnel, including Karnataka State Reserve Police, as a precautionary measure.

updates.text: Sugarcane farmers blocked national highways at several places in Karnataka, demanding higher prices and implementation of the Swaminathan Report.
Farmers participating in the Hubballi Chalo padayatra in Belagavi district are likely to temporarily withdraw their agitation.
